svg.text: Azure AI Native Governance — Architecture (true project content, v1.2)
Version v1.2 • 10 November 2026 • Status: Lab / portfolio • SIMULATED tenant: Nordlicht GmbH • Synthetic data only — no live Azure tenant access
Source of truth: app/data.py + app/checks.py. Every box below is in that code — nothing invented, no service added from the reference picture.
AGENTS — who asks to call a tool (6, from data.py)
FastAPI app — local lab, NOT an Azure service
• Agent registry: 6 agents, every agent has a sponsor (or is blocked)
• OPA server :8181 • 8 Rego policies • Python fallback
• One-shot human-approval queue (exact arguments, one use)
• Tool pinning: SHA-256 hash per tool — a changed tool is denied
• Evidence: SHA-256 hash chain • 6 SQL audit queries
• Audit export: JSON + CSV for Archer / OneTrust (GRC record)
DEMO — what the gateway decides (lab run)
Native decision in every case: none
SIMULATED ESTATE — Nordlicht GmbH (1 subscription, Azure for Students shape, SIMULATED)
vm-web-01, vm-web-02 — encrypted, no public IP
vm-app-01 — disk NOT encrypted, no JIT
vm-db-01 — public IP, no backup, no JIT
vm-test-01 — eastus, public IP, not encrypted
2 VMs with public IP • 2 unencrypted disks
stnordlichtold — PUBLIC blob, NOT encrypted, TLS 1.0
aif-nordlicht (Foundry hub, gpt-4o, EU) — filters on
aoai-test (gpt-4o-mini, US) — NO filter, NO logging
4 expired secrets total • 20 Entra users, 3 without MFA

6 Azure Policy assignments: Allowed locations (Deny) • Storage public blob (Deny) • Require encryption (Audit) • Minimum TLS 1.2 (Deny) • Key Vault purge protection (Audit) • Private endpoints for PaaS (Audit)
Defender for Cloud: secure score 62 / 100 • 14 recommendations open, 5 high severity
10 NATIVE SERVICES — what each CAN and CANNOT decide (from data.py, NATIVE_CAPABILITIES)
CAN: Deny / Audit a resource at creation
CAN: Score the estate, flag, recommend
CAN: RBAC on secrets, expiry, logs
CAN: Logs + alerts — after the fact
CAN: Run an agent with tools + model
CAN: Block a port, private endpoint
Every one of the 10 admits it: no native application decides an individual MCP tool call, checks tool arguments, or approves one specific write.
16 CHECKS AZ-01 – AZ-16 (from app/checks.py — run live, 0 Pass, 8 Fail, 8 Partial)
* AZ-16 is Partial BY DESIGN: it can only become Pass when a gateway like this one is in front of the tools. 28 controls (ISO 42001 + EU AI Act) • 12 risks (R-01 – R-12).
• Evidence register: one SHA-256 hash-chained row per check
• Issues workflow: Open → Verified → Closed (one Issue per Fail)
• Audit export: JSON + CSV for Archer / OneTrust (GRC record)
An agent asks to call a tool (e.g. azure.vm.start).
Gateway checks identity + SHA-256 tool pin + agent allowlist.
OPA decides per call: allow / deny / needs_approval (native: none).
Human approves the write in /approvals — one-shot, exact arguments.
Decision logged as hash-chained evidence — exportable to Archer / OneTrust.
THE GAP — Azure native governs resources, identity, network and model content — NONE of them decides an individual MCP tool call. That is the gap the gateway fills.

What this picture does NOT show (deliberately): no Application Gateway, no Azure Firewall as a deployed resource, no Azure Web App / Function App / Queue service, no Redis, Cosmos DB, SQL Database, Blob or AI Search as separate services,

no VNet topology, no Microsoft Foundry project box, no Foundry Agent Service dependencies box — none of those are in app/data.py or app/checks.py. The gateway is a local-lab FastAPI app, not an Azure service.
Legend: — request / data flow Amber box = gateway decision Red = Fail / blocked Green 1–5 = numbered steps

Azure native applications govern resources, identity, network and model content — none of them decides an individual MCP tool call.
